sources.citation: Eva Rún Guðmundsdóttir. 2013. Með blikk í auga, bros á vör. Rannsókn á því hvort blikk marka skil í íslenska táknmálinu. BA thesis, Háskóli Íslands (Skemman 1946/14999).
sources.note: Prosody-related: blinks as boundary markers in ÍTM narratives. Reviews sign-language prosody (Wilbur 1994, Herrmann 2010: 'hrynjandi, áhersla og hljómfall' = rhythm, stress, intonation; nods/blinks as emphasis markers, p. 11) but makes no statement on where stress falls in ÍTM signs; findings are phrase-boundary level only.

sources.citation: Elísa Guðrún Brynjólfsdóttir, Jóhannes Gísli Jónsson, Kristín Lena Þorvaldsdóttir & Rannveig Sverrisdóttir. 2012. Málfræði íslenska táknmálsins. Íslenskt mál og almenn málfræði 34: 9–52.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: §3 'Hljóðkerfisfræði ÍTM' (pp. 15–21) treats the five parameters (handshape, movement, location, orientation, non-manuals), minimal pairs, distinctive features and the Symmetry/Dominance conditions; nothing on stress or accent. Only prosody remark (p. 15): comparability of spoken and signed phonology is debatable 'e.g. as regards syllables and intonation (atkvæði og hljómfall)'. 'Áhersla' appears only in the pragmatic sense (pronoun/wh-word doubling and EKKI for emphasis, pp. 33, 35, 39).

sources.citation: Elena Koulidobrova & Nedelina Ivanova. 2020. Acquisition of phonology in child Icelandic Sign Language: Unique findings. Proceedings of the Linguistic Society of America 5(1): 164–179. doi:10.3765/plsa.v5i1.4697
sources.note: Non-word repetition and picture-naming study of handshape/orientation/movement/location errors in child ÍTM; cites Brentari's Prosodic Model only as a feature-hierarchy figure. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: SignWiki Ísland. Málfræði íslenska táknmálsins (pointer page to the 2012 article).
sources.note: Only a link to timarit.is page 6620065 for the 2012 article; no content.

sources.citation: Kristín Lena Þorvaldsdóttir. 2011. Sagnir í íslenska táknmálinu. Formleg einkenni og málfræðilegar formdeildir. MA thesis, Háskóli Íslands (Skemman 1946/9997).
sources.note: Verb morphology/syntax thesis; full-text search for áhersl/hrynjand/hljómfall/stress/prosod finds only 'áhersla' as emphasis (pronoun copy, contrastive focus, BIDD as intensifier). No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Nedelina Stoyanova Ivanova. 2008. Tillaga um nýja íslenska táknmálsorðabók á málvísindalegum forsendum. MA thesis, Háskóli Íslands (Skemman 1946/3452).
sources.note: General sign-language phonology chapter (parameters, Movement-Hold model, movement as syllable nucleus). Stress is mentioned only as a spoken-language analogy (Bulgarian minimal pairs by stress position, English noun/verb stress shift) for mouthings and morphological processes; no statement about stress in ÍTM signs.

sources.citation: Nedelina Ivanova (SHH). n.d. On ÍTM – the basics. SignWiki Ísland.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic overview (speaker numbers, legal status, acquisition) with bibliography; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), Icelandic Sign Language; Glottolog 5.1 languoid page icel1236.
sources.note: Wikipedia: 'little research into Icelandic Sign Language's phonology'; lists minimal pairs on all five parameters (from SignWiki); nothing on stress. Glottolog lists the 6 descriptive refs already in the target record.

sources.citation: Kristín Lena Thorvaldsdóttir & Valgerður Stefánsdóttir. 2015. Icelandic Sign Language. In Julie Bakken Jepsen, Goedele De Clerck, Sam Lutalo-Kiingi & William B. McGregor (eds), Sign Languages of the World: A Comparative Handbook, 409–430. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
